Data Collection

Overview

  • Overarching Research Question: Analyze if the ongoing renovation project improved the reliability and performance of the MBTA system. Are there early indicators of significant improvement to the usage and performance of the MBTA system?

  • Goal: Gather and compile datasets relevant to our research question and its sub-questions. We identified reputable data sources and defined our collection methods by choosing an dataset accessed through an API, while finding datasets that have features which fit into requirements of future binary, multivariate, and regression analysis.

  • Motivation:

    • Centralize Data Access: This is a huge project and a tough question to answer! Consolidating datasets to one source not only makes our analysis easier, but also helps Jen and I collaborate.
    • Contextual Insights: We want to collect as much datasets to inform our question. The more, the better. We want to gain a holistic understanding of MBTA from its performance to public perceptions

  • Objectives:

    • Identify and Gather Relevant and Reliable Datasts
    • Ensure Data Coverage (2020-2024)
    • Document data sources
    • Validate data accessibility so recreation is possible

  • Dataset Info:

    • Datasource: MBTA Bluebook Open Data Portal
    • Type: Tabular (.csv)
    • Years: 2020-2024
      • MBTA Service Alerts 2020-2023
      • MBTA Service Alerts 2024
    • Purpose:
      • Analyze causes and effects of service disruptions.
      • Identify routes and stations prone to frequent alerts.
      • Measure severity and frequency of alerts over time.
    • Datasource: Serpapi: Google News Feed
    • Type: Tabular (.json), API
    • Years: 2024
      • Google News Feed
    • Purpose:
      • Understand current public perception through text analysis (sentimen analysis, topic modeling, keyword extraction)
      • Technical use of APIs
    • Datasource: MBTA Bluebook Open Data Portal
    • Type: Tabular (.csv)
    • Years: 2014-2024
      • MBTA The Ride Reliability
    • Purpose:
      • Evlauate long-term trends in service reliability
      • Identify improvements or challenges in accessibility services.
    • Datasource: MBTA Bluebook Open Data Portal
    • Type: Tabular (.json)
    • Years: 2020-2024
      • Rapid Transit and Bus Prediction Accuracy Data
    • Purpose:
      • Find differences between predicted and actual service performance
      • Evalute prediction accuracy trends
    • Datasource: Financial Statements
    • Type: PDF (.json)
    • Years: 2019-2024
      • Financial Statement FY 2019-2024
    • Purpose:
      • Understand macro-level trends in financial trends and whether it correlates with system performance

Data Collection Methods

  • Google News Feed:
    Accessed news feed through the SerpApi Google News API, which tracks real-time and historical collection of news data.

  • MBTA Open Data Portal:
    Datasets, such as service alerts, prediction accuracy, and reliability metrics, were downloaded in tabular formats (.csv and .json) from the MBTA Bluebook Open Data Portal.

  • Financial Data:
    Key financial performance indicators were collected from MBTA’s audited financial reports. They were originally in .pdf formats. Therefore, we used the Camelot library to extract data automatically from PDFs and exported them into .csv format.

Code

Alerts

In the following code, we collected csv files from the MBTA open source data portal. From there, we explored the files manually to see if there are inconsistencies with features or formatting. Thankfully, formatting and information was consistent. Then, we merged the files and added a year column for easy reference in analysis and visualizations. Finally, we used pandas to store collected data as a dataframe.

Why decide to merge all files instead of incrementally cleaning them? I personally found this method to produce less code, which is helpful in large project like this.

What are the drawbacks of this method? Less familiarization with individual datasets.

Merging all existing alert files:

directory_now = '../../data/raw-data/Alerts_2024'
print(os.path.exists(directory_now))    # debug statements 

directory_archive = '../../data/raw-data/Archive_2020-2023'
print(os.path.exists(directory_archive))     # debug statements 

dataframes = [] # list initializaton for dataframes

# function: append files in directories, add the year column
def append_data(directory_path): 
    for foldername, _, filenames in os.walk(directory_path):
        for filename in filenames:
            if filename.endswith('.csv'): 
                file_path = os.path.join(foldername, filename)

                df = pd.read_csv(file_path) # load csv files 

                # Extract the year for yr column, add to dataset
                if '-' in filename:                                 # For 2024 files, due to formatting dif
                    year = int(filename.split('-')[0]) 
                elif '_' in filename:                               # For 2020-2023 files 
                    year = int(filename.split('_')[1]) 
                else:
                    raise ValueError(f"Unexpected filename format: {filename}")
               
                df['year'] = year

                # Append the DataFrames to the list
                dataframes.append(df)

# Load files from directories
append_data(directory_now)
append_data(directory_archive)

# Concatenate all DataFrames into a single DataFrame
merged_data = pd.concat(dataframes, ignore_index=True)

# Save the merged DataFrame to a new CSV file
output_file = '../../data/raw-data/merged_alerts.csv'
merged_data.to_csv(output_file, index=False)

print(f"Output saved as '{output_file}'.")

Current News Media

This script references starter code from Homework 3 DSAN 5000. * Authored by James Hickman. * Modified and extended by Mandy Sun.

# Load API key from personal JSON file
with open('/Users/mandy.sun/Desktop/api_keys/.api-keys.json') as f:
    keys = json.load(f)
API_KEY = keys['serpapi']  # Load SerpApi key from your JSON file

# Define output file for combined results
output_file = '../../data/raw-data/google_news_results.json'

# Define a list of search queries
queries = ["MBTA", "Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority"]

# Store results from both queries
combined_results = []

# Iterate through each query and fetch results from Google News
for query in queries:
    print(f"Performing Google News search for: {query}")
    
    # Define search parameters for Google News
    params = {
        "engine": "google_news",       # Use Google's News search engine
        "q": query,                   # Search query
        "hl": "en",                   # Language: English
        "gl": "us",                   # Geolocation: United States
        "num": 20,                    # Number of results per page
        "api_key": API_KEY            # SerpApi Key
    }
    
    # Fetch search results
    search = GoogleSearch(params)
    result_dict = search.get_dict()

    # Append news results to the combined results list
    combined_results.extend(result_dict.get("news_results", []))

    # Print the news articles to the console
    for result in result_dict.get("news_results", []):
        print(f"Title: {result.get('title')}")
        print(f"Link: {result.get('link')}")
        print(f"Source: {result.get('source')}")
        print("-" * 50)

# Save combined results to a JSON file
with open(output_file, "w") as json_file:
    json.dump(combined_results, json_file, indent=4)

print(f"Combined news data from both queries saved to {output_file}")

Financial Statement

Arguably, the transformation from pdf to csv structured file lies in the intersection of collection and cleaning. However, we will be explaining the transformation into the cleaning page.

Before Transforming:

Below is a linked example of the financial statement pdf file before converting to a structured format (.csv)

View a Financial Statement PDF as an example

Summary

This section will focus on the challenges, benchmarks, and conclusions drawn from our data collection portion. It provides a technical overview on obstacles and limiations with our current dataset. Then, it will provide a brief overview on our next step.

Challenges

Transparency - While the MBTA Open Data Portal provided substantial data in a fairly clean format, there is not transparency about how data is collected by the MBTA. Therefore, we cannot account for biased data (especially since the MBTA is self-reporting). We also do not know if earlier years have incomplete coverage.

  • Financial data only provides aggregated transactional data. We are unable to track individual transactions.

Collection Method Difficulties - Financial data required additional preprocessing as they were available only in PDF format. Converting to structured formats produced difficulties. We initially used pdfplumber library to extract table from pdf file, but failed at integrating it. We then decided on camelot.

  • SerpAPI has rate limits with their basic free plan. Careful management is required when collecting data.

Benchmarks

  • While reliability, ridership details, and accuracy have been datasets explored in the past. Public perception (text analysis on recent news) has rarely been a dataset collected.

Conclusion

Next Step - Following the collection, we will now clean the datasets to ensure it is prime for analysis.

Potential Improvements - Further analysis may cause pivoting in datasts involved. For instance, we may be able to find financial statements that are not aggregated and not in pdf format.

  • It would also be preferrable to track public perceptions from 2020-2024 to track how public perception could have possibly changed through text analysis.
